output:
**Subject: Order TH-48217 – missing delivery and no real resolution**

Good day,

I’m writing about order TH-48217, placed on 21 October and paid for by card: R1,640 including R95 delivery. The order was for six tubs of finger paint, four bags of playdough, 200 paper plates, googly eyes, glitter glue, and two rolls of brown paper. It was for my class at Bergview Pre-Primary in Plumstead, and the delivery address on the order is correct.

Tracking says it was delivered on Tuesday 3 November at 11:42 and signed for by “M. Adams”. There is nobody at our school called M. Adams. Our gate guard, Uncle Faizel, keeps a book of every delivery that comes in, and there is nothing recorded for the 3rd. So the parcel was not delivered to the school, and I don’t know who signed for it, but it wasn’t anyone here.

I emailed on 4 and 6 November and got the same copy-paste reply both times: “we have escalated your query to our courier partner.” I phoned on Friday, spent 38 minutes on hold, and was told nothing can be done until the courier finishes an “investigation” that could take 10 working days. That isn’t acceptable to me. I paid Tiny Hands Edu Supplies, not the courier. I never chose the courier and I have no contract with them. My contract is with you. Asking me to sort it out with the courier is passing your responsibility onto me.

I’m a kindergarten teacher, and this was R1,640 of my own money — on a teacher’s salary — for craft materials for other people’s children. I’ve used you three times before with no issue, which is exactly why this is so frustrating. The kids have already made the mask pattern and I’ve been telling them the paint is “coming soon” for a week. Our end-of-year concert is on 27 November and I need the materials for the props. I can’t keep stalling a class of small children while your courier investigates.

I’m not asking for anything complicated. I want either the order resent in full, or a full refund of R1,640 including the R95 delivery, by Friday 13 November. I also want a proper reply from someone at Tiny Hands who has actually read this email — not another template saying it’s been escalated.

If I don’t have a real answer and a resolution by 13 November, I’ll go ahead with a chargeback through my bank and leave a review explaining what happened. I would much rather sort this out directly with you.

Please confirm receipt of this email and tell me what you are actually doing to fix it.

Kind regards,
[Your name]
[Your phone number / email address]
